reading: Two markers sit on opposite long edges. Each draws a full line across the short dimension in its colour, and the pair of lines repeats with period twice their spacing, alternating colours, until the far edge.

slots.sources: the two markers (first one nearer the start of the long axis)
slots.direction: lines run across the short dimension
slots.period: 2 x distance between the two markers along the long axis

why: every output line is a full row/column in a marker colour, spaced by the marker distance, alternating colours from the first marker onward
invariants: cells before the first marker line stay background

reading: Each red (2) marker gets yellow (4) on its four diagonal neighbours; each blue (1) marker gets orange (7) on its four orthogonal neighbours. Other markers (6, 8) are untouched.
why: around every 2 the four diagonal cells are 4; around every 1 the four orthogonal cells are 7; nothing else changes
invariants: all input cells keep their colour
markers of colours 6 and 8 get nothing

reading: A fixed colour substitution is applied to every cell: 1<->5, 2<->6, 3<->4, 8<->9.
why: each input colour maps to the same output colour on every pair

reading: Pairs of blue (1) markers on opposite borders are joined by a full blue line; every red (2) block the line passes through turns entirely blue.
verb: connect markers and recolour hit blocks

new_rows.name: hit_block
new_rows.datalog:
touch1(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, 2), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, 1).
hit_block(Y, X) :- touch1(O), obj(O, Y, X).

why: each line runs border to border between two same-row/column markers; every 2-object touching a line becomes 1, other 2-objects unchanged
invariants: red blocks not crossed by a line

reading: Each marker draws a full horizontal line at its row; the rows are split into bands (each row goes to the nearest marker, ties to the upper one), and each band gets its marker's colour on the left and right edge columns, with the top and bottom grid rows filled by the first and last band colours.

slots.lines: full-width row at each marker row in its colour
slots.bands: rows assigned to nearest marker row, ties to the upper marker
slots.edges: left/right columns of each band in band colour; row 0 and last row full in first/last band colour

why: every non-background output cell is in a marker row, an edge column, or the top/bottom row, coloured by the band's marker
invariants: interior cells off marker rows stay background

reading: A small multicoloured pattern and a large grey-8 shape that is the pattern scaled up and rotated 90 degrees clockwise. The 8 shape is recoloured block by block with the colours of the rotated pattern; the small pattern stays.
verb: paint scaled shape from rotated exemplar

slots.transform: rotate exemplar 90 degrees clockwise, scale by target size / exemplar size
slots.paint: each scaled block of the target takes the matching rotated-exemplar colour

why: the 8 shape's block mask equals the rotated exemplar's non-background mask, and each block gets that exemplar cell's colour

reading: The input is tiled 2x2, then every coloured cell gets azure (8) on each diagonal neighbour that is background (no wraparound).
why: output is twice the input in each direction; tiled coloured cells stay; a background cell becomes 8 exactly when a diagonal neighbour is coloured
invariants: tiled coloured cells keep their colour (8 never overwrites them)

reading: Three markers form a right triangle. A grey (5) cell is placed at the midpoint of the hypotenuse, and each marker's colour is placed one diagonal step from that midpoint toward that marker.

slots.centre: midpoint of the two markers not at the right angle, coloured 5
slots.copies: each marker colour at centre + sign(marker - centre) in both axes

why: exactly four new cells: 5 at the hypotenuse midpoint and one cell of each marker colour diagonally adjacent to it, pointing to its marker

reading: Every single-colour piece (4-connected) of fewer than 3 cells turns green (3); pieces of 3 or more cells keep their colour.

new_rows.name: small4
new_rows.datalog:
o4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
o4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
same4(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), o4(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
deg(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- same4(Y, X, Y2, X2).
has(Y, X) :- same4(Y, X, Y2, X2).
small4(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !has(Y, X).
small4(Y, X) :- deg(Y, X, N), N = 1, same4(Y, X, Y2, X2), deg(Y2, X2, M), M = 1.

why: a non-background cell becomes 3 iff its 4-connected same-colour component has size 1 or 2; 8-connectivity fails (diagonal contact does not merge)

reading: A full grey (5) wall lines one edge. Every coloured segment sweeps toward the wall in its own colour, each cell's line stopping at the first non-background cell (another segment or the wall), so segments nearer the wall stay on top.
why: from every segment cell a line runs toward the wall over background only and stops just before the first non-background input cell
invariants: cells on the far side of segments from the wall
